questions.question: What question does stratified sampling answer that confidence calibration does not?
options: Is this pipeline good enough to turn automation on in the first place?
Is the pipeline still good, right now, on the documents actually flowing through production?
What should the initial confidence threshold be set to?
How many reviewers should be hired?

questions.question: Why is it critical that stratified sampling include high-confidence, auto-approved extractions and not just low-confidence ones already under review?
options: High-confidence extractions are always wrong, so they need extra scrutiny
A new systematic error pattern could produce high self-reported confidence and sail through auto-approval completely unnoticed otherwise
Low-confidence extractions never need sampling since they're already reviewed
Sampling only high-confidence items is cheaper computationally

questions.question: What kind of real-world change is stratified sampling designed to catch that calibration alone can't anticipate?
options: Changes in reviewer headcount
Drift such as a new vendor layout, OCR degradation, or a model change producing a new error pattern
Changes in the company's org chart
Fluctuations in document file size

questions.question: Which best characterizes the calibration vs. stratified sampling distinction for exam purposes?
options: Calibration = continuous production monitoring; sampling = one-time validation set check
Calibration = static/periodic, done before or independent of live traffic; sampling = continuous, done against live production traffic
They are interchangeable terms for the same process
Calibration only applies to text fields; sampling only applies to numeric fields

questions.question: What is a common concrete stratified sampling pattern mentioned for allocating sample rates?
options: Sample 100% of everything to guarantee no drift is missed
Sample 5-10% of overall volume, weighted more heavily (e.g. 20%) toward higher-risk strata
Sample only once per year regardless of volume
Sample only the lowest-confidence 1% of extractions

questions.question: What's a limitation of stratified sampling even when strata are well-chosen?
options: It cannot detect drift within a document type it already tracks
It only catches drift in the strata being tracked — a genuinely new, unseen document type may not get sampled at the right rate until someone adds it as its own stratum
It requires disabling automation entirely while sampling runs
It is redundant once confidence calibration has been done once
